FIZZUP PARTNER BUSINESS CASE — HUMAN-CURATED VERSION

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
FizzUp is a private AI Speaking Coach for adults who already know English but do not reliably access it under real professional pressure. The product is built around one promise: help a person prepare for, conduct and learn from the conversations that matter. The current system is a real full stack — Flutter mobile client, Node/Fastify/Postgres backend, authentication, personal memory, billing integration and AI voice and text providers. iOS 1.0.0 build 45 passed Apple review. Commercial pricing, paid conversion and learning outcomes beyond current product evidence remain hypotheses.

The proposed partnership is a controlled 90-day enterprise pilot for Polish B1–C1 professionals. FizzUp provides private coaching; the employer receives activation and privacy-safe aggregate outcomes, never individual mistakes, transcripts or private plans. The decision requested by 30 September 2026 is to nominate one sponsor, select a cohort, approve privacy boundaries and agree success and stop criteria.

THE CUSTOMER PROBLEM
Professionals often understand English but underperform in high-stakes meetings, negotiations and presentations. Traditional courses separate practice from the moment of need. Generic AI chat does not preserve a governed learning loop or prove that useful language becomes available later. Employers want improved communication but cannot ethically obtain it through surveillance.

PRODUCT AND USER JOURNEY
1. Prepare — the learner names an upcoming real moment, audience and desired outcome.
2. Speak — a private AI Native conducts a realtime voice exchange calibrated to the situation.
3. Review — the learner sees useful phrases actually used and moments that constrained clarity.
4. Upgrade — FizzUp proposes natural ways to express the same intended meaning more effectively.
5. Practise — the learner actively produces the improved language across varied contexts.
6. Transfer — later sessions test whether the language returns under pressure.
7. Progress — evidence describes observable speaking behavior, not vanity scores.

The product center is voice. Every supporting surface must improve the next conversation, preserve its value or make credible progress visible.

WHAT IS SHIPPED, WHAT IS DIRECTION
Verified today: functioning mobile and backend architecture, authentication, memory mechanisms, billing integration, voice and text provider integrations, and an Apple-reviewed iOS release baseline. Strategic direction: paid tiers, enterprise entitlement, scaled company content and broader automotive or omnichannel continuity. Unproven: willingness to pay, employer conversion, sustained learning transfer and voice-cost economics. These boundaries must remain explicit in every partner claim.

VALUE FOR PARTNERS
Enterprise pilot partners obtain a structured communication-development program without access to private learner content. Distribution partners gain a differentiated adult-learning proposition tied to real work. Content partners can supply governed scenarios and materials without turning FizzUp into a course catalogue. Technology partners can improve voice reliability, latency and cost while respecting tenant and privacy boundaries.

DIFFERENTIATION AND DEFENSIBILITY
FizzUp does not compete on the number of lessons or AI utilities. Its defensibility hypothesis combines a personal relationship with an AI Native, four-layer memory, real-moment context, deliberate language reuse and evidence of transfer. The durable asset is not a transcript archive; it is a privacy-governed model of what helps a particular learner communicate better. Defensibility must be proven through return behavior, successful delayed reuse and partner trust.

COMMERCIAL MODEL — HYPOTHESES
B2C may combine a free activation experience with paid voice capacity, deeper preparation and continuity. B2B may use per-participant program pricing or a cohort pilot fee with clear voice allowances. No price is approved in this report. Every package must be tested against conversion, voice cost, support load, gross margin and retention. The company should avoid unlimited voice promises before provider economics are measured.

GO-TO-MARKET
The initial wedge is adult Polish professionals at B1–C1 with identifiable English moments: customer calls, management meetings, interviews and presentations. Acquire users through professional communities, employer pilots and partners already serving internationalising Polish firms. The first commercial motion should sell a measured pilot outcome, not a broad learning platform. Expansion follows evidence: individual paid conversion, team renewal, new markets and channel partnerships.

SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY
This case uses accepted FizzUp product documentation and the founder brief. It does not rely on invented market statistics, testimonials, interviews or financial history. Product facts are separated from management hypotheses. Decisions are staged through observable evidence: first voice success, completed speaking cycles, delayed phrase reuse, return after a real trigger, privacy-safe pilot activation and willingness to pay.

ASSUMPTIONS AND SCENARIOS
Downside: learners try voice once, do not return, and provider cost remains high. Response: reduce scope, improve first success and stop paid acquisition.
Base: a meaningful segment completes repeated cycles, selected employers sponsor pilots and voice economics support a bounded paid allowance. Response: productise one repeatable cohort offer.
Upside: demonstrated transfer and partner-led distribution create renewals across multiple employers. Response: scale only after privacy and support controls remain effective.
No scenario is a forecast until the financial model is approved and linked to measured cohorts.

90-DAY PILOT
Days 1–30: recruit a narrow cohort, verify first voice success, latency and correct workspace isolation.
Days 31–60: measure completed Prepare–Speak–Review–Practise cycles, return frequency and qualitative usefulness without employer access to private details.
Days 61–90: test willingness to pay, aggregate sponsor reporting, voice cost per active participant and a renewal decision.
Success criteria must be agreed before recruitment. Illustrative gates are activation, repeat speaking, evidence of reuse, sponsor trust and sustainable cost. Final numeric thresholds belong to the signed pilot charter.

RISKS, OWNERS AND CONTROLS
Critical — privacy or tenant leakage. Owner: Privacy Lead. Control: explicit workspace boundary, least privilege, aggregate reporting and incident rehearsal.
High — unreliable realtime voice. Owner: CTO. Control: monitored latency, graceful fallback and provider redundancy plan.
High — weak return behavior. Owner: Product Lead. Control: real-moment onboarding, trigger-based preparation and cohort analysis.
High — unsustainable voice economics. Owner: CFO. Control: allowance design, cost telemetry and scenario limits.
Medium — enterprise complexity before product evidence. Owner: Founder. Control: one narrow pilot contract and fixed customization boundary.

12-MONTH ROADMAP
Quarter 1: first-success reliability, instrumentation and pilot charter.
Quarter 2: controlled employer pilot and pricing tests.
Quarter 3: repeatable onboarding, privacy evidence pack and channel enablement.
Quarter 4: scale decision based on retention, transfer evidence, gross margin and sponsor renewal — or narrow the proposition if evidence is insufficient.

PARTNERSHIP PACKAGES
Pilot sponsor: cohort access, accountable executive and success criteria.
Distribution partner: qualified introductions and joint pilot funnel.
Content partner: governed scenarios linked to real professional moments.
Technology partner: voice, observability or security capability with measurable service levels.
Research partner: independent evaluation of speaking transfer without exposing private learner content.

DECISION AND ASK
Approve one 90-day pilot, not a broad rollout. Nominate an accountable sponsor, agree privacy and evidence boundaries, and set a decision meeting for 30 September 2026. Continue only if users return to meaningful voice, useful language transfers into later speech, partners trust the reporting model and unit economics support a paid service. Otherwise stop, redesign the wedge and preserve the verified product baseline. (explicit-user-brief)

The current system is a real full stack — Flutter mobile client, Node/Fastify/Postgres backend, authentication, personal memory, billing integration and AI voice and text providers. iOS 1.0.0 build 45 passed Apple review. Commercial pricing, paid conversion and learning outcomes beyond current product evidence remain hypotheses.\n\nThe proposed partnership is a controlled 90-day enterprise pilot for Polish B1–C1 professionals. FizzUp provides private coaching; the employer receives activation and privacy-safe aggregate outcomes, never individual mistakes, transcripts or private plans. Traditional courses separate practice from the moment of need. Generic AI chat does not preserve a governed learning loop or prove that useful language becomes available later. Prepare — the learner names an upcoming real moment, audience and desired outcome.\n2. Speak — a private AI Native conducts a realtime voice exchange calibrated to the situation.\n3. Review — the learner sees useful phrases actually used and moments that constrained clarity.\n4. Upgrade — FizzUp proposes natural ways to express the same intended meaning more effectively.\n5. Practise — the learner actively produces the improved language across varied contexts.\n6. Transfer — later sessions test whether the language returns under pressure.\n7. Progress — evidence describes observable speaking behavior, not vanity scores.\n\nThe product center is voice. Every supporting surface must improve the next conversation, preserve its value or make credible progress visible.\n\nWHAT IS SHIPPED, WHAT IS DIRECTION\nVerified today: functioning mobile and backend architecture, authentication, memory mechanisms, billing integration, voice and text provider integrations, and an Apple-reviewed iOS release baseline. Distribution partners gain a differentiated adult-learning proposition tied to real work. Content partners can supply governed scenarios and materials without turning FizzUp into a course catalogue. Technology partners can improve voice reliability, latency and cost while respecting tenant and privacy boundaries.\n\nDIFFERENTIATION AND DEFENSIBILITY\nFizzUp does not compete on the number of lessons or AI utilities. Its defensibility hypothesis combines a personal relationship with an AI Native, four-layer memory, real-moment context, deliberate language reuse and evidence of transfer. Response: productise one repeatable cohort offer.\nUpside: demonstrated transfer and partner-led distribution create renewals across multiple employers. [{"sourceType":"intake","sourceId":"explicit-user-brief","sourceTitle":"Jawny brief użytkownika: Use the following human-curated content as the authoritative source. Preserve its factual boundaries, owners, controls, scenarios and decision ask; improve only structure and readability. Do not add market data, traction, customer evidence or claims not present here.

FIZZUP PARTNER BUSINESS CASE — HUMAN-CURATED VERSION

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
FizzUp is a private AI Speaking Coach for adults who already know English but do not reliably access it under real professional pressure. The product is built around one promise: help a person prepare for, conduct and learn from the conversations that matter. The current system is a real full stack — Flutter mobile client, Node/Fastify/Postgres backend, authentication, personal memory, billing integration and AI voice and text providers. iOS 1.0.0 build 45 passed Apple review. Commercial pricing, paid conversion and learning outcomes beyond current product evidence remain hypotheses.

The proposed partnership is a controlled 90-day enterprise pilot for Polish B1–C1 professionals. FizzUp provides private coaching; the employer receives activation and privacy-safe aggregate outcomes, never individual mistakes, transcripts or private plans. The decision requested by 30 September 2026 is to nominate one sponsor, select a cohort, approve privacy boundaries and agree success and stop criteria.

THE CUSTOMER PROBLEM
Professionals often understand English but underperform in high-stakes meetings, negotiations and presentations. Traditional courses separate practice from the moment of need. Generic AI chat does not preserve a governed learning loop or prove that useful language becomes available later. Employers want improved communication but cannot ethically obtain it through surveillance.

PRODUCT AND USER JOURNEY
1. Prepare — the learner names an upcoming real moment, audience and desired outcome.
2. Speak — a private AI Native conducts a realtime voice exchange calibrated to the situation.
3. Review — the learner sees useful phrases actually used and moments that constrained clarity.
4. Upgrade — FizzUp proposes natural ways to express the same intended meaning more effectively.
5. Practise — the learner actively produces the improved language across varied contexts.
6. Transfer — later sessions test whether the language returns under pressure.
7. Progress — evidence describes observable speaking behavior, not vanity scores.

The product center is voice. Every supporting surface must improve the next conversation, preserve its value or make credible progress visible.

WHAT IS SHIPPED, WHAT IS DIRECTION
Verified today: functioning mobile and backend architecture, authentication, memory mechanisms, billing integration, voice and text provider integrations, and an Apple-reviewed iOS release baseline. Strategic direction: paid tiers, enterprise entitlement, scaled company content and broader automotive or omnichannel continuity. Unproven: willingness to pay, employer conversion, sustained learning transfer and voice-cost economics. These boundaries must remain explicit in every partner claim.

VALUE FOR PARTNERS
Enterprise pilot partners obtain a structured communication-development program without access to private learner content. Distribution partners gain a differentiated adult-learning proposition tied to real work. Content partners can supply governed scenarios and materials without turning FizzUp into a course catalogue. Technology partners can improve voice reliability, latency and cost while respecting tenant and privacy boundaries.

DIFFERENTIATION AND DEFENSIBILITY
FizzUp does not compete on the number of lessons or AI utilities. Its defensibility hypothesis combines a personal relationship with an AI Native, four-layer memory, real-moment context, deliberate language reuse and evidence of transfer. The durable asset is not a transcript archive; it is a privacy-governed model of what helps a particular learner communicate better. Defensibility must be proven through return behavior, successful delayed reuse and partner trust.

COMMERCIAL MODEL — HYPOTHESES
B2C may combine a free activation experience with paid voice capacity, deeper preparation and continuity. B2B may use per-participant program pricing or a cohort pilot fee with clear voice allowances. No price is approved in this report. Every package must be tested against conversion, voice cost, support load, gross margin and retention. The company should avoid unlimited voice promises before provider economics are measured.

GO-TO-MARKET
The initial wedge is adult Polish professionals at B1–C1 with identifiable English moments: customer calls, management meetings, interviews and presentations. Acquire users through professional communities, employer pilots and partners already serving internationalising Polish firms. The first commercial motion should sell a measured pilot outcome, not a broad learning platform. Expansion follows evidence: individual paid conversion, team renewal, new markets and channel partnerships.

SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY
This case uses accepted FizzUp product documentation and the founder brief. It does not rely on invented market statistics, testimonials, interviews or financial history. Product facts are separated from management hypotheses. Decisions are staged through observable evidence: first voice success, completed speaking cycles, delayed phrase reuse, return after a real trigger, privacy-safe pilot activation and willingness to pay.

ASSUMPTIONS AND SCENARIOS
Downside: learners try voice once, do not return, and provider cost remains high. Response: reduce scope, improve first success and stop paid acquisition.
Base: a meaningful segment completes repeated cycles, selected employers sponsor pilots and voice economics support a bounded paid allowance. Response: productise one repeatable cohort offer.
Upside: demonstrated transfer and partner-led distribution create renewals across multiple employers. Response: scale only after privacy and support controls remain effective.
No scenario is a forecast until the financial model is approved and linked to measured cohorts.

90-DAY PILOT
Days 1–30: recruit a narrow cohort, verify first voice success, latency and correct workspace isolation.
Days 31–60: measure completed Prepare–Speak–Review–Practise cycles, return frequency and qualitative usefulness without employer access to private details.
Days 61–90: test willingness to pay, aggregate sponsor reporting, voice cost per active participant and a renewal decision.
Success criteria must be agreed before recruitment. Illustrative gates are activation, repeat speaking, evidence of reuse, sponsor trust and sustainable cost. Final numeric thresholds belong to the signed pilot charter.

RISKS, OWNERS AND CONTROLS
Critical — privacy or tenant leakage. Owner: Privacy Lead. Control: explicit workspace boundary, least privilege, aggregate reporting and incident rehearsal.
High — unreliable realtime voice. Owner: CTO. Control: monitored latency, graceful fallback and provider redundancy plan.
High — weak return behavior. Owner: Product Lead. Control: real-moment onboarding, trigger-based preparation and cohort analysis.
High — unsustainable voice economics. Owner: CFO. Control: allowance design, cost telemetry and scenario limits.
Medium — enterprise complexity before product evidence. Owner: Founder. Control: one narrow pilot contract and fixed customization boundary.

12-MONTH ROADMAP
Quarter 1: first-success reliability, instrumentation and pilot charter.
Quarter 2: controlled employer pilot and pricing tests.
Quarter 3: repeatable onboarding, privacy evidence pack and channel enablement.
Quarter 4: scale decision based on retention, transfer evidence, gross margin and sponsor renewal — or narrow the proposition if evidence is insufficient.

PARTNERSHIP PACKAGES
Pilot sponsor: cohort access, accountable executive and success criteria.
Distribution partner: qualified introductions and joint pilot funnel.
Content partner: governed scenarios linked to real professional moments.
Technology partner: voice, observability or security capability with measurable service levels.
Research partner: independent evaluation of speaking transfer without exposing private learner content.

DECISION AND ASK
Approve one 90-day pilot, not a broad rollout. Nominate an accountable sponsor, agree privacy and evidence boundaries, and set a decision meeting for 30 September 2026. Continue only if users return to meaningful voice, useful language transfers into later speech, partners trust the reporting model and unit economics support a paid service. Otherwise stop, redesign the wedge and preserve the verified product baseline."}]

FIZZUP PARTNER BUSINESS CASE — HUMAN-CURATED VERSION

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
FizzUp is a private AI Speaking Coach for adults who already know English but do not reliably access it under real professional pressure. The product is built around one promise: help a person prepare for, conduct and learn from the conversations that matter. The current system is a real full stack — Flutter mobile client, Node/Fastify/Postgres backend, authentication, personal memory, billing integration and AI voice and text providers. iOS 1.0.0 build 45 passed Apple review. Commercial pricing, paid conversion and learning outcomes beyond current product evidence remain hypotheses.

The proposed partnership is a controlled 90-day enterprise pilot for Polish B1–C1 professionals. FizzUp provides private coaching; the employer receives activation and privacy-safe aggregate outcomes, never individual mistakes, transcripts or private plans. The decision requested by 30 September 2026 is to nominate one sponsor, select a cohort, approve privacy boundaries and agree success and stop criteria.

THE CUSTOMER PROBLEM
Professionals often understand English but underperform in high-stakes meetings, negotiations and presentations. Traditional courses separate practice from the moment of need. Generic AI chat does not preserve a governed learning loop or prove that useful language becomes available later. Employers want improved communication but cannot ethically obtain it through surveillance.

PRODUCT AND USER JOURNEY
1. Prepare — the learner names an upcoming real moment, audience and desired outcome.
2. Speak — a private AI Native conducts a realtime voice exchange calibrated to the situation.
3. Review — the learner sees useful phrases actually used and moments that constrained clarity.
4. Upgrade — FizzUp proposes natural ways to express the same intended meaning more effectively.
5. Practise — the learner actively produces the improved language across varied contexts.
6. Transfer — later sessions test whether the language returns under pressure.
7. Progress — evidence describes observable speaking behavior, not vanity scores.

The product center is voice. Every supporting surface must improve the next conversation, preserve its value or make credible progress visible.

WHAT IS SHIPPED, WHAT IS DIRECTION
Verified today: functioning mobile and backend architecture, authentication, memory mechanisms, billing integration, voice and text provider integrations, and an Apple-reviewed iOS release baseline. Strategic direction: paid tiers, enterprise entitlement, scaled company content and broader automotive or omnichannel continuity. Unproven: willingness to pay, employer conversion, sustained learning transfer and voice-cost economics. These boundaries must remain explicit in every partner claim.

VALUE FOR PARTNERS
Enterprise pilot partners obtain a structured communication-development program without access to private learner content. Distribution partners gain a differentiated adult-learning proposition tied to real work. Content partners can supply governed scenarios and materials without turning FizzUp into a course catalogue. Technology partners can improve voice reliability, latency and cost while respecting tenant and privacy boundaries.

DIFFERENTIATION AND DEFENSIBILITY
FizzUp does not compete on the number of lessons or AI utilities. Its defensibility hypothesis combines a personal relationship with an AI Native, four-layer memory, real-moment context, deliberate language reuse and evidence of transfer. The durable asset is not a transcript archive; it is a privacy-governed model of what helps a particular learner communicate better. Defensibility must be proven through return behavior, successful delayed reuse and partner trust.

COMMERCIAL MODEL — HYPOTHESES
B2C may combine a free activation experience with paid voice capacity, deeper preparation and continuity. B2B may use per-participant program pricing or a cohort pilot fee with clear voice allowances. No price is approved in this report. Every package must be tested against conversion, voice cost, support load, gross margin and retention. The company should avoid unlimited voice promises before provider economics are measured.

GO-TO-MARKET
The initial wedge is adult Polish professionals at B1–C1 with identifiable English moments: customer calls, management meetings, interviews and presentations. Acquire users through professional communities, employer pilots and partners already serving internationalising Polish firms. The first commercial motion should sell a measured pilot outcome, not a broad learning platform. Expansion follows evidence: individual paid conversion, team renewal, new markets and channel partnerships.

SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY
This case uses accepted FizzUp product documentation and the founder brief. It does not rely on invented market statistics, testimonials, interviews or financial history. Product facts are separated from management hypotheses. Decisions are staged through observable evidence: first voice success, completed speaking cycles, delayed phrase reuse, return after a real trigger, privacy-safe pilot activation and willingness to pay.

ASSUMPTIONS AND SCENARIOS
Downside: learners try voice once, do not return, and provider cost remains high. Response: reduce scope, improve first success and stop paid acquisition.
Base: a meaningful segment completes repeated cycles, selected employers sponsor pilots and voice economics support a bounded paid allowance. Response: productise one repeatable cohort offer.
Upside: demonstrated transfer and partner-led distribution create renewals across multiple employers. Response: scale only after privacy and support controls remain effective.
No scenario is a forecast until the financial model is approved and linked to measured cohorts.

90-DAY PILOT
Days 1–30: recruit a narrow cohort, verify first voice success, latency and correct workspace isolation.
Days 31–60: measure completed Prepare–Speak–Review–Practise cycles, return frequency and qualitative usefulness without employer access to private details.
Days 61–90: test willingness to pay, aggregate sponsor reporting, voice cost per active participant and a renewal decision.
Success criteria must be agreed before recruitment. Illustrative gates are activation, repeat speaking, evidence of reuse, sponsor trust and sustainable cost. Final numeric thresholds belong to the signed pilot charter.

RISKS, OWNERS AND CONTROLS
Critical — privacy or tenant leakage. Owner: Privacy Lead. Control: explicit workspace boundary, least privilege, aggregate reporting and incident rehearsal.
High — unreliable realtime voice. Owner: CTO. Control: monitored latency, graceful fallback and provider redundancy plan.
High — weak return behavior. Owner: Product Lead. Control: real-moment onboarding, trigger-based preparation and cohort analysis.
High — unsustainable voice economics. Owner: CFO. Control: allowance design, cost telemetry and scenario limits.
Medium — enterprise complexity before product evidence. Owner: Founder. Control: one narrow pilot contract and fixed customization boundary.

12-MONTH ROADMAP
Quarter 1: first-success reliability, instrumentation and pilot charter.
Quarter 2: controlled employer pilot and pricing tests.
Quarter 3: repeatable onboarding, privacy evidence pack and channel enablement.
Quarter 4: scale decision based on retention, transfer evidence, gross margin and sponsor renewal — or narrow the proposition if evidence is insufficient.

PARTNERSHIP PACKAGES
Pilot sponsor: cohort access, accountable executive and success criteria.
Distribution partner: qualified introductions and joint pilot funnel.
Content partner: governed scenarios linked to real professional moments.
Technology partner: voice, observability or security capability with measurable service levels.
Research partner: independent evaluation of speaking transfer without exposing private learner content.

DECISION AND ASK
Approve one 90-day pilot, not a broad rollout. Nominate an accountable sponsor, agree privacy and evidence boundaries, and set a decision meeting for 30 September 2026. Continue only if users return to meaningful voice, useful language transfers into later speech, partners trust the reporting model and unit economics support a paid service. ## Executive Summary

_Purpose: Top-level synthesis with the decision or recommendation._

## Executive Summary

FizzUp is a private AI Speaking Coach tailored for adults who possess English proficiency but face challenges in utilizing it effectively under professional pressure. The platform is committed to helping users prepare for, conduct, and learn from significant conversations. It boasts a comprehensive full-stack architecture, including a Flutter mobile client, Node/Fastify/Postgres backend, authentication, personal memory, billing integration, and AI voice and text providers. The iOS application has successfully passed Apple's review. While commercial pricing, paid conversion, and learning outcomes are still hypotheses, the system is poised for a controlled enterprise pilot.

> **NOTE:** Key Decision Request: Approve the initiation of a controlled 90-day enterprise pilot aimed at Polish professionals with B1–C1 English proficiency. This decision involves nominating an accountable sponsor, selecting a participant cohort, agreeing on privacy boundaries, and establishing success and termination criteria. The deadline for this decision is set for 30 September 2026.

## Problem Statement

_Purpose: Substantive section "Problem Statement" relevant to the document goal._

## Problem Statement

Many professionals possess a working knowledge of English but struggle to demonstrate effective communication skills during high-pressure professional events such as meetings, negotiations, and presentations. This gap often leads to underperformance, despite their language proficiency. Traditional language courses are inadequate as they separate learning from the moment of need, failing to provide the immediate application required in real-world scenarios.

- Traditional courses fail to integrate practice into real-world scenarios where immediate application is necessary.
- Generic AI solutions lack a governed learning loop to ensure that improvement in language skills carries over after sessions.
- Employers need better communication efficacy without relying on privacy-invasive measures.

> **NOTE:** Professionals often struggle to perform effectively in high-stakes English-speaking situations such as meetings, negotiations, and presentations, despite having a good understanding of the language. Traditional language courses fail to integrate practice with real-time needs, and generic AI chat solutions do not ensure that learned language skills are retained and accessible when required. Employers are keen to enhance their employees' communication skills but face ethical challenges, as surveillance-based methods compromise privacy and trust.

## Proposed Initiative

_Purpose: Substantive section "Proposed Initiative" relevant to the document goal._

## Proposed Initiative

- Prepare: Learners identify a pivotal future moment and desired communication outcome.
- Speak: Engage in a tailored voice interaction guided by the AI Native.
- Review: Examine language used and identify clarity challenges in communication.
- Upgrade: Receive suggestions on more effective language expressions.
- Practise: Practice the enhanced language across varied situations.
- Transfer: Validate language retention in subsequent pressured scenarios.
- Progress: Track improvement through demonstrated communication behavior.

The proposed 90-day pilot in Poland is designed to validate the efficacy of FizzUp as a personalized AI speaking coach for Polish professionals at B1–C1 English proficiency levels. The initiative aims to deliver private coaching while safeguarding privacy and providing aggregate reporting to employers. Key objectives include verifying initial voice success, assessing completed user journey cycles, and evaluating participants' willingness to pay. Success metrics will encompass user engagement, language reuse, partner trust, and voice economics, which will inform the decision to scale, continue, or modify the initiative.

> **NOTE:** The decision to proceed with the pilot is contingent upon several critical factors: ensuring users consistently engage in meaningful voice interactions, observing successful language transfer into subsequent professional scenarios, maintaining partner trust in the reporting model, and establishing a sustainable cost structure that supports the service's long-term viability.

## Economic Analysis

_Purpose: Substantive section "Economic Analysis" relevant to the document goal._

## Economic Analysis

In evaluating the economic feasibility of FizzUp, two commercial models are considered: business-to-consumer (B2C) and business-to-business (B2B). Each model presents distinct assumptions and challenges. For B2C, the key assumption is that users will be attracted to a free activation phase, with paid features such as enhanced voice capacity and comprehensive preparation being critical to conversion. Voice cost is a significant factor, necessitating careful monitoring to ensure profitability. In the B2B model, pricing could involve per-participant program fees or a cohort pilot pricing. Here, assumptions include employer willingness to invest in pilot programs and the capacity of the voice economics to support a bounded paid allowance. Each scenario will require rigorous testing against conversion rates, support load, and gross margins before wide-scale deployment.

| model | voiceCost | conversion | retention |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free Activation + Paid Voice Capacity | Medium | High | Moderate |
| Enhance Package Prep | High | Moderate | Low |
| Per-Participant Program Fee | Low | High | High |
| Cohort Pilot Pricing | Medium | Moderate | Moderate |

## Benefits and KPIs

_Purpose: Substantive section "Benefits and KPIs" relevant to the document goal._

## Benefits and KPIs

- Access to a cutting-edge AI-driven speaking coach for professional development.
- Privacy-guaranteed program ensuring no personal mistakes or private plans are shared.
- Structured communication-development program with measurable outcomes.
- Enhanced communication skills for partner employees, leading to improved business interactions.
- Opportunity to shape the future roadmap and influence the direction of the AI speaking coach.

## Risks

_Purpose: Substantive section "Risks" relevant to the document goal._

## Risks

| Risk | Owner | Control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Privacy or tenant leakage | Privacy Lead | Explicit workspace boundary, least privilege, aggregate reporting and incident rehearsal |
| Unreliable realtime voice | CTO | Monitored latency, graceful fallback and provider redundancy plan |
| Weak return behavior | Product Lead | Real-moment onboarding, trigger-based preparation and cohort analysis |
| Unsustainable voice economics | CFO | Allowance design, cost telemetry and scenario limits |
| Enterprise complexity before product evidence | Founder | One narrow pilot contract and fixed customization boundary |

> **NOTE:** Addressing privacy or tenant leakage risks and ensuring reliable realtime voice processing are paramount. Privacy concerns are managed by the Privacy Lead through explicit workspace boundaries, least privilege access, aggregate reporting, and incident rehearsals. Unreliable realtime voice processing, managed by the CTO, is mitigated through monitored latency, graceful fallback mechanisms, and a provider redundancy plan. These issues can significantly impact user trust and platform effectiveness if unresolved. Continuous monitoring and strategic controls are essential to maintain user confidence and operational integrity.

## Implementation Outline

_Purpose: Substantive section "Implementation Outline" relevant to the document goal._

## Implementation Outline

1. Days 1–30: Recruit a narrow cohort focusing on a specific group of Polish B1–C1 professionals. Verify the success of initial voice interactions and ensure the workspace provides proper isolation to maintain privacy.
2. Days 31–60: Monitor the completion of Prepare–Speak–Review–Practise cycles. Measure return frequency and gauge qualitative feedback, ensuring that employers do not access private learner details.
3. Days 61–90: Evaluate participants' willingness to pay and provide aggregate reporting to sponsors. Analyze voice costs per active participant and determine whether to proceed with a renewal decision based on predefined success criteria.

## Recommendation

_Purpose: Substantive section "Recommendation" relevant to the document goal._

## Recommendation

A managed pilot is recommended to evaluate the FizzUp AI Speaking Coach's effectiveness for Polish B1–C1 professionals. This controlled environment allows for precise monitoring of voice success, language transfer, and partner trust within a specific cohort, avoiding the risks associated with a broad rollout. The pilot will test key hypotheses regarding willingness to pay and voice cost economics, providing essential data on user engagement, language improvement, and economic viability. This focused approach ensures informed decision-making for potential future expansions.

> **NOTE:** To proceed with expansion, it is crucial that users consistently return to the service and effectively apply learned language in real-world scenarios. Partner confidence in data reporting and robust unit economics must be confirmed. If these criteria are unmet, the strategy should be reassessed, refining the offering to preserve the product's verified core functionality while addressing any identified gaps.

## Appendix

_Purpose: Substantive section "Appendix" relevant to the document goal._

## Appendix

This appendix provides a comprehensive overview of FizzUp's technical framework and strategic direction. FizzUp is an AI-powered platform designed to improve English speaking skills for professionals, especially in high-stakes situations. The platform's architecture is built on a full-stack solution, integrating a Flutter mobile client with a Node/Fastify/Postgres backend, ensuring robust performance and user engagement. Strategic initiatives focus on expanding enterprise capabilities and refining AI-driven feedback to enhance user satisfaction and relevance. These initiatives are supported by controlled pilot programs that test product hypotheses, ensuring privacy and cost-effectiveness while delivering measurable outcomes. The strategic direction prioritizes partner trust and positions FizzUp as a reliable solution in the language learning market. This appendix highlights ongoing efforts to optimize product offerings and provide a scalable, consistent solution for business partners and users.

Strategic direction: paid tiers, enterprise entitlement, scaled company content and broader automotive or omnichannel continuity. Unproven: willingness to pay, employer conversion, sustained learning transfer and voice-cost economics. These boundaries must remain explicit in every partner claim.

VALUE FOR PARTNERS
Enterprise pilot partners obtain a structured communication-development program without access to private learner content. Distribution partners gain a differentiated adult-learning proposition tied to real work. Content partners can supply governed scenarios and materials without turning FizzUp into a course catalogue. Technology partners can improve voice reliability, latency and cost while respecting tenant and privacy boundaries.

DIFFERENTIATION AND DEFENSIBILITY
FizzUp does not compete on the number of lessons or AI utilities. Its defensibility hypothesis combines a personal relationship with an AI Native, four-layer memory, real-moment context, deliberate language reuse and evidence of transfer. The durable asset is not a transcript archive; it is a privacy-governed model of what helps a particular learner communicate better. Defensibility must be proven through return behavior, successful delayed reuse and partner trust.

COMMERCIAL MODEL — HYPOTHESES
B2C may combine a free activation experience with paid voice capacity, deeper preparation and continuity. B2B may use per-participant program pricing or a cohort pilot fee with clear voice allowances. No price is approved in this report. Every package must be tested against conversion, voice cost, support load, gross margin and retention. The company should avoid unlimited voice promises before provider economics are measured.

GO-TO-MARKET
The initial wedge is adult Polish professionals at B1–C1 with identifiable English moments: customer calls, management meetings, interviews and presentations. Acquire users through professional communities, employer pilots and partners already serving internationalising Polish firms. The first commercial motion should sell a measured pilot outcome, not a broad learning platform. Expansion follows evidence: individual paid conversion, team renewal, new markets and channel partnerships.

SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY
This case uses accepted FizzUp product documentation and the founder brief. It does not rely on invented market statistics, testimonials, interviews or financial history. Product facts are separated from management hypotheses. Decisions are staged through observable evidence: first voice success, completed speaking cycles, delayed phrase reuse, return after a real trigger, privacy-safe pilot activation and willingness to pay.

ASSUMPTIONS AND SCENARIOS
Downside: learners try voice once, do not return, and provider cost remains high. Response: reduce scope, improve first success and stop paid acquisition.
Base: a meaningful segment completes repeated cycles, selected employers sponsor pilots and voice economics support a bounded paid allowance. Response: productise one repeatable cohort offer.
Upside: demonstrated transfer and partner-led distribution create renewals across multiple employers. Response: scale only after privacy and support controls remain effective.
No scenario is a forecast until the financial model is approved and linked to measured cohorts.

90-DAY PILOT
Days 1–30: recruit a narrow cohort, verify first voice success, latency and correct workspace isolation.
Days 31–60: measure completed Prepare–Speak–Review–Practise cycles, return frequency and qualitative usefulness without employer access to private details.
Days 61–90: test willingness to pay, aggregate sponsor reporting, voice cost per active participant and a renewal decision.
Success criteria must be agreed before recruitment. Illustrative gates are activation, repeat speaking, evidence of reuse, sponsor trust and sustainable cost. Final numeric thresholds belong to the signed pilot charter.

RISKS, OWNERS AND CONTROLS
Critical — privacy or tenant leakage. Owner: Privacy Lead. Control: explicit workspace boundary, least privilege, aggregate reporting and incident rehearsal.
High — unreliable realtime voice. Owner: CTO. Control: monitored latency, graceful fallback and provider redundancy plan.
High — weak return behavior. Owner: Product Lead. Control: real-moment onboarding, trigger-based preparation and cohort analysis.
High — unsustainable voice economics. Owner: CFO. Control: allowance design, cost telemetry and scenario limits.
Medium — enterprise complexity before product evidence. Owner: Founder. Control: one narrow pilot contract and fixed customization boundary.

12-MONTH ROADMAP
Quarter 1: first-success reliability, instrumentation and pilot charter.
Quarter 2: controlled employer pilot and pricing tests.
Quarter 3: repeatable onboarding, privacy evidence pack and channel enablement.
Quarter 4: scale decision based on retention, transfer evidence, gross margin and sponsor renewal — or narrow the proposition if evidence is insufficient.

Pilot sponsor: cohort access, accountable executive and success criteria.
Distribution partner: qualified introductions and joint pilot funnel.
Content partner: governed scenarios linked to real professional moments.
Technology partner: voice, observability or security capability with measurable service levels.
Research partner: independent evaluation of speaking transfer without exposing private learner content.

DECISION AND ASK
Approve one 90-day pilot, not a broad rollout. Nominate an accountable sponsor, agree privacy and evidence boundaries, and set a decision meeting for 30 September 2026. Continue only if users return to meaningful voice, useful language transfers into later speech, partners trust the reporting model and unit economics support a paid service. Otherwise stop, redesign the wedge and preserve the verified product baseline. (explicit-user-brief)

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
FizzUp is a private AI Speaking Coach for adults who already know English but do not reliably access it under real professional pressure. The product is built around one promise: help a person prepare for, conduct and learn from the conversations that matter. The current system is a real full stack — Flutter mobile client, Node/Fastify/Postgres backend, authentication, personal memory, billing integration and AI voice and text providers. iOS 1.0.0 build 45 passed Apple review. Commercial pricing, paid conversion and learning outcomes beyond current product evidence remain hypotheses.

The proposed partnership is a controlled 90-day enterprise pilot for Polish B1–C1 professionals. FizzUp provides private coaching; the employer receives activation and privacy-safe aggregate outcomes, never individual mistakes, transcripts or private plans. The decision requested by 30 September 2026 is to nominate one sponsor, select a cohort, approve privacy boundaries and agree success and stop criteria.

THE CUSTOMER PROBLEM
Professionals often understand English but underperform in high-stakes meetings, negotiations and presentations. Traditional courses separate practice from the moment of need. Generic AI chat does not preserve a governed learning loop or prove that useful language becomes available later. Employers want improved communication but cannot ethically obtain it through surveillance.

PRODUCT AND USER JOURNEY
1. Prepare — the learner names an upcoming real moment, audience and desired outcome.
2. Speak — a private AI Native conducts a realtime voice exchange calibrated to the situation.
3. Review — the learner sees useful phrases actually used and moments that constrained clarity.
4. Upgrade — FizzUp proposes natural ways to express the same intended meaning more effectively.
5. Practise — the learner actively produces the improved language across varied contexts.
6. Transfer — later sessions test whether the language returns under pressure.
7. Progress — evidence describes observable speaking behavior, not vanity scores.

The product center is voice. Every supporting surface must improve the next conversation, preserve its value or make credible progress visible.

WHAT IS SHIPPED, WHAT IS DIRECTION
Verified today: functioning mobile and backend architecture, authentication, memory mechanisms, billing integration, voice and text provider integrations, and an Apple-reviewed iOS release baseline. Strategic direction: paid tiers, enterprise entitlement, scaled company content and broader automotive or omnichannel continuity. Unproven: willingness to pay, employer conversion, sustained learning transfer and voice-cost economics. These boundaries must remain explicit in every partner claim.

VALUE FOR PARTNERS
Enterprise pilot partners obtain a structured communication-development program without access to private learner content. Distribution partners gain a differentiated adult-learning proposition tied to real work. Content partners can supply governed scenarios and materials without turning FizzUp into a course catalogue. Technology partners can improve voice reliability, latency and cost while respecting tenant and privacy boundaries.

DIFFERENTIATION AND DEFENSIBILITY
FizzUp does not compete on the number of lessons or AI utilities. Its defensibility hypothesis combines a personal relationship with an AI Native, four-layer memory, real-moment context, deliberate language reuse and evidence of transfer. The durable asset is not a transcript archive; it is a privacy-governed model of what helps a particular learner communicate better. Defensibility must be proven through return behavior, successful delayed reuse and partner trust.

COMMERCIAL MODEL — HYPOTHESES
B2C may combine a free activation experience with paid voice capacity, deeper preparation and continuity. B2B may use per-participant program pricing or a cohort pilot fee with clear voice allowances. No price is approved in this report. The initial wedge is adult Polish professionals at B1–C1 with identifiable English moments: customer calls, management meetings, interviews and presentations. Expansion follows evidence: individual paid conversion, team renewal, new markets and channel partnerships.

SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY
This case uses accepted FizzUp product documentation and the founder brief. It does not rely on invented market statistics, testimonials, interviews or financial history. No scenario is a forecast until the financial model is approved and linked to measured cohorts.

The durable asset is not a transcript archive; it is a privacy-governed model of what helps a particular learner communicate better. Defensibility must be proven through return behavior, successful delayed reuse and partner trust.

COMMERCIAL MODEL — HYPOTHESES
B2C may combine a free activation experience with paid voice capacity, deeper preparation and continuity. B2B may use per-participant program pricing or a cohort pilot fee with clear voice allowances. No price is approved in this report. Every package must be tested against conversion, voice cost, support load, gross margin and retention. The company should avoid unlimited voice promises before provider economics are measured.

GO-TO-MARKET
The initial wedge is adult Polish professionals at B1–C1 with identifiable English moments: customer calls, management meetings, interviews and presentations. Acquire users through professional communities, employer pilots and partners already serving internationalising Polish firms. The first commercial motion should sell a measured pilot outcome, not a broad learning platform. Expansion follows evidence: individual paid conversion, team renewal, new markets and channel partnerships.

SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY
This case uses accepted FizzUp product documentation and the founder brief. It does not rely on invented market statistics, testimonials, interviews or financial history. Product facts are separated from management hypotheses. Decisions are staged through observable evidence: first voice success, completed speaking cycles, delayed phrase reuse, return after a real trigger, privacy-safe pilot activation and willingness to pay.

ASSUMPTIONS AND SCENARIOS
Downside: learners try voice once, do not return, and provider cost remains high. Response: reduce scope, improve first success and stop paid acquisition.
Base: a meaningful segment completes repeated cycles, selected employers sponsor pilots and voice economics support a bounded paid allowance. Response: productise one repeatable cohort offer.
Upside: demonstrated transfer and partner-led distribution create renewals across multiple employers. Response: scale only after privacy and support controls remain effective.
No scenario is a forecast until the financial model is approved and linked to measured cohorts.

90-DAY PILOT
Days 1–30: recruit a narrow cohort, verify first voice success, latency and correct workspace isolation.
Days 31–60: measure completed Prepare–Speak–Review–Practise cycles, return frequency and qualitative usefulness without employer access to private details.
Days 61–90: test willingness to pay, aggregate sponsor reporting, voice cost per active participant and a renewal decision.
Success criteria must be agreed before recruitment. Illustrative gates are activation, repeat speaking, evidence of reuse, sponsor trust and sustainable cost. Final numeric thresholds belong to the signed pilot charter.

RISKS, OWNERS AND CONTROLS
Critical — privacy or tenant leakage. Owner: Privacy Lead. Control: explicit workspace boundary, least privilege, aggregate reporting and incident rehearsal.
High — unreliable realtime voice. Owner: CTO. Control: monitored latency, graceful fallback and provider redundancy plan.
High — weak return behavior. Owner: Product Lead. Control: real-moment onboarding, trigger-based preparation and cohort analysis.
High — unsustainable voice economics. Owner: CFO. Control: allowance design, cost telemetry and scenario limits.
Medium — enterprise complexity before product evidence. Owner: Founder. Control: one narrow pilot contract and fixed customization boundary.

12-MONTH ROADMAP
Quarter 1: first-success reliability, instrumentation and pilot charter.
Quarter 2: controlled employer pilot and pricing tests.
Quarter 3: repeatable onboarding, privacy evidence pack and channel enablement.
Quarter 4: scale decision based on retention, transfer evidence, gross margin and sponsor renewal — or narrow the proposition if evidence is insufficient.

PARTNERSHIP PACKAGES
Pilot sponsor: cohort access, accountable executive and success criteria.
Distribution partner: qualified introductions and joint pilot funnel.
Content partner: governed scenarios linked to real professional moments.
Technology partner: voice, observability or security capability with measurable service levels.
Research partner: independent evaluation of speaking transfer without exposing private learner content.

DECISION AND ASK
Approve one 90-day pilot, not a broad rollout. Nominate an accountable sponsor, agree privacy and evidence boundaries, and set a decision meeting for 30 September 2026. Continue only if users return to meaningful voice, useful language transfers into later speech, partners trust the reporting model and unit economics support a paid service. Otherwise stop, redesign the wedge and preserve the verified product baseline."}],"assumptions":["Sekcja "Benefits and KPIs", blok 149beafa-5935-4c83-a90e-135c1c565338: treść oznaczona jako założenie do weryfikacji."],"risks":["1/27 bloków oznaczonych jako założenie (isAssumption) — brak podpiętego źródła."],"confidence":"medium","toVerify":["Sekcja "Benefits and KPIs" wymaga treści/źródeł (obecnie założenie/stub)."]},"owner":"3ef1b819-31f6-40a3-a77a-47d2a4436fbb"}
